42380663.t: Spatial remodeling of bone marrow architecture defines tissue-state signatures of disease activity and therapeutic response in MDS
42380663.sum: Whole-slide multiplex immunofluorescence with single-cell phenotyping of more than 5 million cells from MDS marrow biopsies: diagnostic (n=36), longitudinal (n=29), precursor (n=13) and normal (n=21).
f: MDS shows genotype-imprinted remodeling: altered progenitor patterning, disrupted erythroid islands, HSPCs displaced from perivascular niches.
An 82-feature Microarchitectural Perturbation Score (MDS-MAPS) separated remission from active disease better than blast percentage (AUC 0.883 vs 0.660).
It also separated low-blast MDS from CCUS (AUC 0.815), normalized in remission and re-emerged at relapse.
42380663.why: A template for linking spatial features of the marrow to disease activity and therapy response in MDS.

42239259.t: Niche-level immune evasion in TP53-mutant AML residual disease revealed by spatial proteomics
42239259.sum: Sequential immunofluorescence on whole bone marrow biopsies from TP53-wild-type and TP53-mutant AML, at diagnosis and in morphological complete remission. Mutant cells were identified by high p53 and mapped against stromal and immune niches.
f: At remission, TP53-mutant marrow shows B-cell loss and more regulatory T cells.
Erythroid and immature leukemia clusters persist in perisinusoidal niches, apart from T-cell clusters.
FOXP3-high Tregs sit close to mutant MRD cells.
scRNA-seq points to an erythroid to T-cell GDF15–CD48 axis as the suppression route.
42239259.why: Spatial marrow map of AML tied to residual disease and relapse risk, the closest match to your project.

42816584.t: Prefibrotic bone marrow microenvironment is a hallmark of clonal hematopoiesis
42816584.sum: scRNA-seq, histology and spatial transcriptomics of human marrow with clonal hematopoiesis (CHIP).
f: Fibro-inflammatory remodeling with expanded CAF-like fibroblasts and higher collagen and ECM programs.
Spatial fiber-enriched hubs contain CXCL12+ fibroblasts, macrophages and lymphoid cells, with TGF-β and TNF signaling.
Niche changes appear before overt malignancy.
42816584.why: Shows that the niche is altered before leukemia, a useful reference for pre-malignant states.

42855473.t: Mitochondria transfer via tunneling nanotubes drives macrophage immunosuppression and metabolic reprogramming in pediatric AML
42855473.sum: Princess Máxima Center study of how pediatric AML cells reprogram macrophages in the marrow.
f: Immunosuppressive macrophages dominate the pediatric AML microenvironment (RUNX1::RUNX1T1, KMT2A-rearranged).
AML cells switch macrophages to an anti-inflammatory state (NF-κB suppression) by direct contact and tunneling-nanotube transfer of mitochondria, rewiring OXPHOS.
Reprogrammed macrophages show impaired phagocytosis, chemoresistance, and reduced T-cell and bispecific-antibody killing.
42855473.why: A pediatric AML niche mechanism involving macrophages, which a CODEX panel could look for in situ.

42122217.t: A three-gene interferon signature predicts sustained complete remission in pediatric AML
42122217.sum: 32 pediatric AML samples at diagnosis (NanoString IO360, RNA-seq, flow cytometry), validated in the TARGET cohort.
f: The interferon signature tracks chemosensitivity, lower MRD and longer overall survival, also within standard-risk patients.
It is linked to non-exhausted CD4 and CD8 cytotoxic cells and CD8 TEMRA cells.
42122217.why: Connects immune state at diagnosis to outcome in children.

42830144.t: Reactive oxygen species define leukemia stem cell identity in pediatric AML
42830144.sum: Pediatric AML cells were sorted by ROS level and tested for stemness, niche behavior and metabolism, including in mice and a 3D niche model.
f: ROS-low cells are quiescent, form colonies serially and engraft in mice.
In the 3D niche model they settle in hypoxic regions and resist cytarabine.
Low oxidative phosphorylation, yet they depend on complex I.
A ROS-low gene signature finds stem cells in scRNA-seq data and is prognostic.
42830144.why: Links stem cell state to hypoxic niche location in children.

42836918.t: Menin inhibition in pediatric UBTF-TD myelodysplastic syndrome
42836918.sum: A single child with MDS with excess blasts and a UBTF tandem duplication, a high-risk pediatric MDS/AML subtype with a HOX/MEIS1 program.
f: Revumenib added to azacitidine and venetoclax led to transfusion independence and clearance of blasts and the UBTF-TD clone.
The child then had allogeneic transplant and was in complete remission at one year.
One case, so hypothesis-generating only.
42836918.why: Pediatric MDS genetics and a new targeted option, but one patient only.

42360909.t: FGF18 mediates fibroblast–leukemia cross talk to promote AML progression
42360909.sum: scRNA-seq of the AML marrow niche, fibroblast-specific knockout, a CRISPR screen in AML cells and a neutralizing antibody in mice.
f: Stromal fibroblasts upregulate Fgf18; deleting it delays disease and extends survival.
FGF18 acts through FGFR3, AKT–mTOR and IL-6, which feeds back on fibroblast JAK–STAT3.
The loop suppresses CD8+ T-cell function.
High FGF18 predicts poor prognosis; the antibody restores CD8 function and adds to anti-PD-1.
42360909.why: A defined stromal cell to leukemia signaling loop, tested in vivo.

42847991.t: Latexin deletion in the bone marrow niche suppresses leukemia via LIFR downregulation and immune activation
42847991.sum: MLL-AF9 AML transplanted into Lxn-knockout recipient mice, with stromal scRNA-seq.
f: Lxn-knockout recipients live longer and have fewer LSCs and blasts.
Lower LIFR signaling in MSCs raises Cxcl9 and recruits more cytotoxic CD8 T cells.
Adding anti-PD-1 prolongs survival further.
42847991.why: A good template for niche-focused murine validation, which is your aim 3.

42871763.t: Immune and cellular determinants of response to HMA-venetoclax in AML
42871763.sum: 132 patients with clinical and genomic data, plus scRNA-seq and TCR sequencing in 10 patients.
f: Responders have expanded cytotoxic CD8 T cells, higher TCR diversity and antigen-presentation activation.
Non-responders show inflammatory signaling, impaired myeloid maturation, an IDO1+ dendritic-cell-rich suppressive niche and a stem-like, EMT state.
LAG-3 marks dysfunctional T cells and is a candidate biomarker or target.
42871763.why: Ties marrow immune composition to therapy response, the question in your aim 2.

42856304.t: Clonally expanded CD8 T cells in AML adopt an NK-like program
42856304.sum: Mass cytometry of 46 diagnostic AML marrows plus scRNA-seq and TCR sequencing.
f: CD8 T cells skew to TEMRA; classic exhaustion is rare.
TEMRA cells are functional (IFNγ and TNFα).
The most expanded clones, of unknown specificity, express NK receptors (LaNKi score), validated in other datasets.
42856304.why: Describes the T-cell states you would see in a marrow CODEX panel.

42883947.t: Inflammatory network remodeling in AML is driven by neutrophil-centric self-amplifying circuits
42883947.sum: scRNA-seq of 3 AML and 6 donor samples with CellChat, plus Luminex cytokines in 46 AML and 26 controls.
f: Communication shifts from T cells toward myeloid cells and neutrophils (CXCL8–CXCR2, CCL3–CCR1).
An inflammatory risk score (CXCL8, CCL2, IL-1A; C-index 0.729) splits ELN2022 intermediate risk.
Very small scRNA-seq cohort.
42883947.why: Cytokine-based risk readout, though the single-cell cohort is small.

42782774.t: Targeting TGFBR1 with TP-6379 improves hematopoiesis in low-risk MDS ex vivo
42782774.sum: Primary low-risk MDS marrow cells treated with the ALK5-specific inhibitor TP-6379, plus S100A9-transgenic mice.
f: S100A9-driven inflammation and TGFβ impair MDS hematopoiesis.
TP-6379 restored hematopoiesis, especially in spliceosome-mutant samples, and rescued the S100A9 effect.
Validated in S100A9-transgenic mice.
42782774.why: MDS niche inflammation with a murine model.

42876702.t: T cells form distinct spatially restricted immune responses in synovium of psoriatic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis
42876702.sum: High-multiplex IHC on synovial biopsies with neighborhood analysis around lining fibroblasts.
f: In PsA, Th1 and Th17 cells sit closest to fibroblasts, then Th2 and Th9.
In RA, Th9, Th17 and Th22 form the barrier.
Methotrexate is linked to about 50% fewer Th cells nearby.
42876702.why: A multiplexed imaging immunology paper with stromal-centered neighborhood analysis and a treatment comparison.

42882852.t: Single-cell and multi-omics profiling of the multiple myeloma immune niche
42882852.sum: Review of spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging of the myeloma marrow.
f: Immune exclusion, stromal support and metabolic niches shape the marrow.
CAR-T and T-cell-engager response depends on spatial accessibility, antigen retention and myeloid suppression.
Proposes a spatial-temporal framework for progression and relapse.
42882852.why: Overview of how spatial data is being used in another marrow cancer.

42657369.t: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells are functionally remodeled after complete remission of AML
42657369.sum: Marrow MSCs from de novo AML, AML in complete remission and healthy donors, with an AML remission mouse model.
f: Dysfunctional AML MSCs recover in remission and resemble healthy MSCs.
Fewer senescent MSCs after remission.
Remission MSCs can still be pushed back into senescence by AML cells.
42657369.why: Shows the stroma is plastic and tracks disease state.

42439614.sum: Narrative review of inflammation in MDS.
f: Chronic inflammation and inflammaging drive clonal selection and niche remodeling.
TP53 and spliceosome mutations amplify inflammatory signaling and reshape the niche.
Peripheral blood inflammatory indices correlate with prognosis and therapy response.
42439614.why: Background for the MDS niche and why inflammation matters.

42084223.t: CellFuse enables multimodal integration of single-cell and spatial proteomics data for systems-level analysis in cancer
42084223.sum: Supervised contrastive learning framework that integrates cytometry, CITE-seq and spatial proteomics even when few markers are shared.
f: Accurate cross-modality label transfer that outperforms existing methods in blood, bone marrow and lymphoma, including rare subsets.
In solid tumors it reconstructs spatial microenvironments whose interactions correlate with treatment response.
42084223.why: Directly useful for combining CODEX-type data with flow or CITE-seq.

42957737.t: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric AML
42957737.sum: Single-cell transcriptomes of paired diagnosis and relapse samples were used to infer chemoresistant populations, then combined with cytogenetics and MRD after induction.
f: Nearly 40% of pediatric AML patients relapse and die.
The combined approach finds a group of 20% of patients not transplanted in first remission, with 5-year event-free survival below 40% and almost half of the deaths.
Chemoresistant populations show therapeutic vulnerabilities for high-risk disease.
42957737.why: Pediatric AML with outcome-linked single-cell data and better risk groups, the same kind of link you want from spatial data.

42848511.t: Sorafenib enhances graft-versus-leukemia activity through IL-18-mediated macrophage and NK cell crosstalk in FLT3-ITD AML
42848511.sum: scRNA-seq of the marrow immune microenvironment in FLT3-ITD AML patients receiving sorafenib after allogeneic transplant, with mouse experiments.
f: Sorafenib promotes macrophage to NK cell crosstalk through IL-18, raising NK cytotoxicity and graft-versus-leukemia effect.
It inhibits mitochondrial complexes I and V, which raises IL-18 production (PKM2–RelA) and release through caspase-3/GSDME pyroptosis in macrophages.
42848511.why: Drug effect on the marrow immune niche, with macrophage and NK cell interaction.

42895851.t: RUNX1-ETO oncoprotein levels determine the balance between endothelial reprogramming and pre-leukemic growth in a human ES cell model of AML
42895851.sum: Human embryonic stem cell line with inducible RUNX1-ETO, analyzed by single-cell methods.
f: RUNX1-ETO reprograms ESC-derived myeloid progenitors toward endothelial cells, depending on its level and irreversibly.
A subpopulation of blood progenitors escapes reprogramming and keeps proliferating when co-cultured with endothelial cells.
Cell-cell interactions maintain pre-leukemic cells.
42895851.why: t(8;21) is common in children, and this shows how endothelial interactions support pre-leukemic cells.

42637517.t: Single-cell chromatin profiling reveals relapse-related priming in pediatric AML
42637517.sum: scATAC-seq of 177,500 cells from 16 diagnostic pediatric AML samples (t(8;21), inv(16), FLT3-ITD) with long-term outcome, comparing relapsed and non-relapsed patients.
f: Relapse-linked chromatin signatures are visible at diagnosis across subtypes.
Higher innate immune and inflammatory activation, and more HSC/MPP-like leukemic progenitors.
AP-1, RUNX1, SPI1 and ETS motifs drive the relapse state, and their high expression predicts worse survival in other AML cohorts.

41874448.t: Same-slide spatial multiomics with IN-DEPTH reveals tumor virus-linked reorganization of the microenvironment
41874448.sum: Single-cell spatial proteomics imaging guides spatial transcriptomic capture on the same slide without RNA loss. A graph method (SGCC) links protein and RNA layers. Tested on EBV-positive and EBV-negative DLBCL.
f: Protein-first design keeps epitopes, RNA quality and tissue intact on commercial platforms.
Found coordinated tumor, macrophage and CD4 T-cell remodeling, C1Q-high suppressive macrophages and a candidate IL27–STAT3 axis.
41874448.why: One way to add transcriptomics to multiplexed protein imaging.

42957952.t: Intravital imaging of early AML expansion in the mouse calvarial bone marrow
42957952.sum: Step-by-step protocols for tracking early HoxA9-Meis1 AML expansion relative to local bone remodeling in live mouse calvaria.
f: Leukemic cells expanded almost only in marrow cavities undergoing active bone remodeling.
Protocols cover labeling, imaging of leukemia, vasculature and bone remodeling together, plus image analysis.
Can be combined with spatially resolved tissue isolation and sequencing.
42957952.why: Murine in vivo imaging of the AML niche, useful for your functional validation work.

42998044.t: Distinct consequences of BCOR and BCORL1 mutations in myeloid neoplasms and bone marrow failure
42998044.sum: Analysis of 11,340 patients, 418 with BCOR/BCORL1 mutations, with single-cell DNA sequencing and longitudinal data.
f: In myeloid neoplasms the mutations are usually secondary and linked to older age and worse survival; in marrow failure they are primary and not prognostic.
BCOR/L1-mutant clones often shrink over time; progression tracks with extra mutations, especially RUNX1.
In marrow failure they tend to predict a good response to immunosuppression; BCOR loss lowers HLA class I, hinting at immune privilege.
42998044.why: Genetic context for MDS and marrow failure that overlaps with pediatric disease.
